name: Ramana Kumar Vinjamuri
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering
fitReason: A computational HRI and assistive-robot option combining pretrained visual perception, compact movement representations and physical humanoid interaction. Stronger in multimodal interface integration and dimensionality reduction than foundation-model policy learning.

physicalEvidence.summary: The May 4, 2026 SIVAM paper documents MediaPipe pose/hand streams retargeted through inverse kinematics and scaled joint mapping to actual Unitree G1 and Mitra robots. Its five-person technical pilot was conducted February–July 2025; biosignal-driven visuals used prerecorded signals, so it does not establish live affect-adaptive control or clinical benefit. A separate November 24, 2025 Scientific Reports study combines MediaPipe, Gaussian-modeled velocities, PCA synergies and sparse reconstruction, mapping hand postures onto Mitra’s five-DoF hand. That evaluation covers static end postures rather than dynamic sequences and manually adjusts out-of-plane poses. Current lab membership and a December 2025 university report independently establish the group’s physical hands/humanoids and student attribution.

shortVisit.summary: No current external-master’s short-visit invitation was verified on the lab or faculty pages. The member list includes a 2019 visiting graduate researcher, but that predates the lab’s August 2020 move from Stevens to UMBC and is historical precedent only.

unknowns: Reuse the separately documented UMBC policy: Research Scholar requires an already-earned master’s and Faculty/Fellow appointment; the Short-Term Scholar degree threshold is unclear. A continuing master’s student is not automatically eligible.

UMBC’s $2,200/$2,300 monthly support-page conflict and distinct Student category funding rules remain unresolved. Personal bank statements for a scholar do not establish an eligible self-funded student visit.

The verified work is technical perception/retargeting and representation learning. It should not be described as validated emotion inference, a clinical treatment, a fully learned motion policy or autonomous dance therapy.
